editorial.marketOverview: Friday's shortened session saw Nasdaq rise 2.31% and SOX about 4.7%, while AP reports Russell 2000 up 1.7%, consistent with broad participation. The weekly rebound was strong but holiday liquidity and the preceding selloff limit trend inference. Weekly breadth is unusually broad, but the Nasdaq's 6.7% weekly gain only partly offsets the preceding 10% decline.
editorial.whatChanged: Latest repository early outlook at 02:41 ET retains score -12 and consolidation risk 16/100. Open Watch remains updated 02:31 UTC with no new curated catalyst. MarketWatch reports 97% of S&P constituents advanced over the week, and AP reports Russell 2000 gained 6.5% over the week. These are additional historical breadth confirmations, not new trading. No material change to the three-session path.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The rebound remains a relief move pending normal-liquidity confirmation. Cooling volatility is constructive, but VXN remains elevated. Repository yields of 4.936% and 4.710% imply 22.6 basis points; WSJ reports slightly earlier lower yields and a widely priced December hike. Oil settlements remain historical and weekend supply risks prospective. The weekly breadth confirmation reduces concern that the rebound was confined to one AI stock, without resolving the rate or financing headwinds.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday tests Friday's broad rally under normal liquidity after OPEC+; Rubrik reports after close. Tuesday ISM and JOLTS at 10 ET may reset rate expectations, with Marvell and Credo guidance after close shaping Wednesday's chip trade. Wednesday ADP and the semiconductor earnings response are the main in-horizon tests; Salesforce and Snowflake report after close. Thursday's reported Huang testimony may influence positioning before the event, not an observed reaction.
editorial.bullCase: Broad participation and sustained semiconductor relative strength, combined with easing volatility and stable or lower yields, could extend Friday's rebound. Constructive chip guidance would reinforce the demand narrative.
editorial.bearCase: A reversal in chip leadership, renewed oil supply disruption or yields above 5% could unwind the relief rally. Weak AI infrastructure guidance or hotter macro data could intensify valuation pressure.
editorial.watchNext: Watch Sunday OPEC+ decision and futures reopening, Monday breadth and synchronized rates/volatility, Tuesday macro and chip earnings, Wednesday ADP. Reuters dates Huang Senate testimony to Thursday December 3; Friday payrolls and December 8–9 Fed meeting are also outside the horizon but may affect positioning.
